original_test_intent: Verify approved IIO Configuration values persist and restore to SPEC while every expected PCIe root port, switch, retimer and endpoint remains on the correct socket/lane route at required generation/width with no new AER or boot fault.
original_method: Freeze BIOS/CPU/socket and complete PCIe route oracle; preserve AER/SEL/kernel evidence; select a reversible dependency-aware IIO value or coherent bifurcation group; use KVM to change, save/reboot and verify retained page; compare every root-port/switch/retimer/endpoint BDF, identity, generation/width, NUMA/socket affinity, driver and AER delta; apply Load Defaults and repeat; stop on missing/moved/downgraded endpoint, surprise removal, AER burst or no-boot and use owner-controlled known-good/CMOS recovery.
manual_activity: A qualified operator changes only approved IIO controls through KVM, performs save/reboot and Load Defaults checkpoints, captures pages and keeps physical recovery available.
required_inputs: BIOS/CPU/socket identity and full root-port/switch/retimer/endpoint/lane topology
IIO defaults and safe values with bifurcation/routing dependencies and expected effects
Per-path BDF/device/gen/width/affinity/driver/AER acceptance and boot timing
Maintenance, workload drain, KVM, known-good settings and CMOS/physical recovery ownership
safety_requirements: Never apply all/random IIO values; validate lane ownership, bifurcation and endpoint compatibility
Preserve AER/SEL/kernel logs and baseline topology; do not clear evidence
Drain affected PCIe workloads and verify every sibling path after each change
Stop on endpoint loss/move, link downgrade, driver failure, AER/surprise-removal delta, hang or no-boot
Do not retrain/reset devices, auto-reboot/retry or clear CMOS
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, IIO matrix, dependencies, topology oracle, maintenance and recovery
Guide operator checkpoints and collect screenshots plus complete PCIe route/link/driver/AER evidence
Compare retained and restored states with SPEC without issuing verdict
Do not choose settings, clear logs, manipulate BIOS/PCIe reset/retrain or invoke recovery
engineer_actions: Approve exact IIO page/defaults and reversible routing/bifurcation matrix
Approve full PCIe route/gen/width/affinity/driver/error criteria and recovery
Review page, boot, topology and AER evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

review_improvement: Adds complete IIO route and sibling-link validation, preventing a retained menu value from hiding missing or degraded PCIe devices and avoiding unsafe random lane mappings.
independent_technical_reasoning: IIO settings directly determine PCIe lane ownership and routing. A system can boot with a wrong bifurcation while a GPU, NIC or storage endpoint disappears or trains narrow/slow. Thus every approved change must be checked against the board-specific full path oracle, including siblings and AER deltas. Because a wrong value can remove boot or management endpoints before OS access, execution remains manually supervised with physical recovery.
